YEAR BOOK AND OFFICIAL ROSTER OF THE YMCAs OF NORTH AMERICA — the volumes for 1906, 1907 and 1908
Internet Archive: ymcayearbookof1906younuoft / ...1907... / ...1908...

NONE IS LENDING-RESTRICTED. All three djvu texts were downloaded whole (1.17 MB, 1.15 MB, 1.11 MB)
and searched. "Kanawana" occurs ZERO times in any of them — expected, since the present site opens
in 1910 and this series rosters STAFF, not programmes.

CAUTION ON THE DATE. The Internet Archive gives 1890 as the year for every University of Toronto
scan in this series. The year here is taken from the identifier. See p_433.

WHY THESE THREE. p_433 named 1906-1908 as the volumes to take next, because they sit either side of
W. H. Ball Jr.'s departure (1901/02) and just before the camp's move to Saint-Sauveur (1910).

    Holliday, W. J., Montreal, Que., Asst., 06        (1906 volume)
    Holliday, W. J., Montreal, Que., Boys, 06         (1907 and 1908 volumes)
    Budge, D. A., Montreal, Que., Sec., 74            (all three)


WHAT FOLLOWS
------------

**W. J. HOLLIDAY WAS THE ASSOCIATION'S BOYS' WORK SECRETARY, AND HE STARTED IN 1906.** He is the man
the association's own 1931 report calls "W. J. HOLLIDAY, THE FIRST CAMP DIRECTOR", and whose charge
of the new Saint-Sauveur site the 1910 annual report announces in the forward tense. This project's
directors index has him as "1908, 1910-1912?". He enters Association work in 1906 as an Assistant
Secretary and is BOYS' WORK DIRECTOR from the 1907 volume — so when he ran the Junior Camp at Lac
St. Joseph in 1908 and opened Kanawana in 1910, he was doing it as the association's boys' work
secretary and not as a seasonal appointment.

**JOHN W. ROSS WAS PRESIDENT OF THE YMCA OF MONTREAL** in all three years. This project has him as
chairman of the 1894 Summer Camp committee, as volunteer chairman of a mid-1890s Junior Department
camp committee, on the 1899 Permanent Camp Committee (f_4908), and on the YMCA International
Committee in 1921 with a term expiring in 1922 (f_4964). The presidency joins those into one
forty-year public life, and it bears on billy-ball.md's open question 8 — whether "John W. Ross" and
"John Roy", the 1901 Camp Jubilee director, are one man or two.

**W. H. BALL, JR. IS GONE.** Physical Director in every volume 1893-97, absent from all three of
these, where the post is J. E. Merritt's. Consistent with the 1901/1902 departure this project has
from the annual reports, and the first outside confirmation of it.

**W. S. MAGUIRE, and a thread not pulled.** He is Montreal's Assistant Physical Director in the 1908
volume. The 1921 volume has "Physical, W. S. Maguire" at VICTORIA, B.C., on the same four-line
roster as "Boys, Harold C. Cross" (f_4965). A Montreal physical director and a Montreal boys' work
man in the same small western association thirteen years later. NO CLAIM IS MADE that one brought
the other; it is a documented co-occurrence, and the sort of thing that would explain how Cross got
to Victoria and back if anyone can date Maguire's move.

**J. E. MERRITT**, Physical Director in all three, turns up again in 1912 on the "Programme des
Amusements" committee of Montreal's first child-welfare exhibition, alongside C. B. Powter and
D. J. Evans (f_4961).


AND A METHOD NOTE THAT COST SOMETHING
-------------------------------------
The p_430 name sweep ran "W.J. Holliday" against the Open Library full-text index on 2026-09-06,
got 243 hits about an Indianapolis art collector and an Indianapolis steel company, and logged him
in the sweep file as "do not re-run bare". He was in a reference series ALREADY SITTING IN THIS
REPO'S CACHE, under his own name, with his job title and his start year.

That is rule 21 for the second time in an hour — a source marked READ is read FOR SOMETHING — and
this time it is aimed at the name sweep's own method. **Before running a name against a corpus of
millions of books, grep the cache.** It takes one command and it is where this project's own
reading already is.
